articles.headline: Premier League live updates: Chelsea host Man United in early matchup
articles.description: We've got plenty of treats in store on Halloween, starting with Chelsea against Manchester United to kick off a packed day of action. United have brought captain Bruno Fernandes back into the team.
articles.headlineJa: プレミアリーグ速報：チェルシーがマン・ユナイテッドをホームに迎える初戦
articles.descriptionJa: ハロウィンらしく、盛りだくさんの試合が用意されています。まずはチェルシー対マンチェスター・ユナイテッドの試合から幕を開けます。ユナイテッドはキャプテンのブルーノ・フェルナンデスを先発に復帰させました。
articles.body:
Happy Halloween! It's the final day of October, but there's still plenty of exciting matches to look forward to as we kick off a packed weekend of action across Europe.

We get things started in the Premier League, where Chelsea host an inconsistent Manchester United side, with head coach Michael Carrick under mounting pressure to turn things around.

Later there are seven more games, highlighted by a clash between two in-form sides as Manchester City face Brighton & Hove Albion, just three days after their Carabao Cup encounter. We then round off the day with a London derby as Tottenham Hotspur take on Crystal Palace, before Aston Villa take on Fulham.

Elsewhere across Europe, Atlético Madrid face Levante in LaLiga, while the Bundesliga serves up a blockbuster Der Klassiker between league leaders Bayern Munich, led by newly crowned Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane, and second-placed Borussia Dortmund.

Follow along for all the latest goals, updates and highlights from Saturday's matches.

articles.headline: Bruno Fernandes returns to Man United XI for Chelsea clash
articles.description: Bruno Fernandes has returned to the Manchester United starting lineup.
articles.headlineJa: ブルーノ・フェルナンデス、チェルシー戦でマン・ユナイテッドの先発メンバーに復帰
articles.descriptionJa: ブルーノ・フェルナンデスがマンチェスター・ユナイテッドのスタメンに復帰しました。
articles.body:
Bruno Fernandes has returned to the Manchester United starting lineup following a fallout with manager Michael Carrick and captains the side in their Premier League clash against Chelsea.

Carrick has recalled Fernandes after holding "clear-the-air" talks with the Portugal midfielder following his criticism of Carrick's tactics at United.

Fernandes was left on the bench in last weekend's defeat to Bournemouth at Old Trafford.

Carrick handed Harry Maguire the captain's armband in his absence.

The Red Devils have failed to win in eight of their last games in all competitions. They have suffered five defeats and three draws. Their last victory came against Sabah in the Champions League on Sept. 1.

Despite the run of poor form, United boss Carrick has kept the faith of the club hierarchy, saying he was "not surprised" to have been left in charge for the crunch game at Stamford Bridge.

To face Chelsea, Carrick has called upon Lisandro Martínez in place of Ayden Heaven while Matheus Cunha replaces Mason Mount and Fernandes takes the spot of Youri Tielemans.

There was also a notable inclusion in the hosts' team as Xabi Alonso named the previously out-of-favour Estêvão in the Chelsea starting XI. 

Cole Palmer returned to the team after missing the midweek Carabao Cup defeat to Liverpool due to the red card he was shown against Tottenham Hotspur last weekend.

- Youri Tielemans backs Michael Carrick at Man United: 'We don't want a big change'

- Man United's Michael Carrick and Bruno Fernandes hold 'clear-the-air' talks - reports 

- Harry Maguire: Man United players are 'fully behind' Michael Carrick

Chelsea team

Starting XI: Mike Penders, Josh Acheampong, Wesley Fofana, Levi Colwill, Pedro Neto, Moisés Caicedo, Romeo Lavia, Marco Palestra, Estêvão, Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers. 

Substitutes: Teddy Sharman-Lowe, Valentín Barco, Pep Chavarría, Emmanuel Emegha, Olutayo Subuloye, Malo Gusto, Mahdi Nicoll-Jazuli, Danny Welbeck, Geovany Quenda.

Man United team

Starting XI: Sanne Lammens, Leny Yoro, Harry Maguire, Lisandro Martínez, Diogo Dalot, Andrey Santos, Carlos Baleba, Amad Diallo, Bruno Fernandes, Matheus Cinha, Bryan Mbeumo. 

Substitutes: Karl Darlow, Ayden Heaven, Shea Lacey, Kobbie Mainoo, Noussair Mazraoui, Mason Mount, Youri Tielemans, Joshua Zirkzee, Matthijs de Ligt.

articles.headline: 'No way' that Jets trade star WR Garrett Wilson before deadline, source says
articles.description: The Jets are not expected to trade Garrett Wilson, sources told ESPN, despite increased speculation about the star wide receiver's future.
articles.headlineJa: ジェッツが期限前にスターWRギャレット・ウィルソンをトレードする可能性は「あり得ない」と関係者が語る
articles.descriptionJa: スターワイドレシーバーの将来に関する憶測が高まっているものの、ジェッツがギャレット・ウィルソンをトレードする見込みはないと、関係者がESPNに語りました。
articles.body:
As trade talks ramp up across the NFL, there is one player who isn't going anywhere before the deadline despite increased speculation: New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson.

One well-placed source told ESPN this weekend that there is "no way" the Jets will trade Wilson by the NFL's Nov. 10 trade deadline, despite any interest from other teams.

The Jets might have said the same thing a year ago in regard to cornerback Sauce Gardner and defensive tackle Quinnen Williams, only to trade both on deadline day for a bevy of draft picks.

But sources said the situation this year with Wilson is different for various reasons.

The Tennessee Titans told teams there was no way they would trade perennial Pro Bowl defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons -- until they did Thursday, when they received two first-round picks and a fourth-round pick from the Chicago Bears. But Wilson does seem untouchable before the deadline.

For starters, the Jets have no interest in moving on from Wilson, 26, who is considered to be one of the most talented wide receivers in the NFL. The Jets signed him to a four-year, $130 million extension that runs through 2030 a mere 15 months ago.

Additionally, Jets ownership is said to love Wilson and would want no part of trading him, according to sources.

The Jets already have amassed a surplus of draft picks -- the Indianapolis Colts' 2027 first-round pick and the higher of Dallas' or Green Bay's 2027 first-round pick -- in exchange for Gardner and Williams. At some point, New York needs to prioritize making picks, not accumulating them.

That is the exact plan with Wilson, who is viewed as a central building block as the Jets look to replenish their roster and get stronger on offense in the 2027 draft.

Wilson recently told reporters that he did not want to be traded.

"I want to be here, man," he said. "I want to win games, and that's the one thing we've been missing on here. I love it here. Do I love it more than I love winning? Nah, to be completely honest, but I'm hopeful.

"I've never been the best optimistic guy, but I've found a way and dug deep, and I've been optimistic for three, four, five years now. And that's why these [losses] each weekend hurt a little more."

Other wide receiver names continue to come up in connection to the trade deadline: Jacksonville's Brian Thomas Jr., Indianapolis' Josh Downs, Minnesota's Jauan Jennings, Cleveland's Jerry Jeudy, Tennessee's Calvin Ridley and even Wilson.

The other receivers might be attainable in the days leading up to the Nov. 10 trade deadline, but Wilson is not.

articles.headline: Sources: Colts willing to trade RB Jonathan Taylor, active in talks with teams
articles.description: The Colts now are open to trading Jonathan Taylor, sources told ESPN and NFL Network, and multiple teams have reached out to Indianapolis.
articles.headlineJa: 関係者：コルツはRBジョナサン・テイラーの放出を検討中、他チームとの交渉も進行中
articles.descriptionJa: コルツがジョナサン・テイラーのトレードに前向きであることを関係者がESPNとNFL Networkに明かしており、複数のチームがインディアナポリスに接触しています。
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts now are open to trading star running back Jonathan Taylor, sources told ESPN and NFL Network.

Multiple teams have reached out to Indianapolis, and those talks are said to be active and ongoing, according to sources.

The list of teams that have expressed at least some level of interest in trading for Taylor is thought to include the Denver Broncos, Green Bay Packers, Minnesota Vikings, New York Giants and Seattle Seahawks, sources said.

Colts owner and CEO Carlie Irsay-Gordon and Taylor met this week and had what sources described as an in-depth conversation to discuss the future. Irsay-Gordon is said to have an affinity for the three-time Pro Bowler, and the Colts would prefer for Taylor to be a part of their rebuild.

But the Colts also recognize the potential haul Taylor could bring in a trade.

In 2022, the San Francisco 49ers traded second-, third-, fourth- and fifth-round draft picks to the Carolina Panthers for running back Christian McCaffrey. The Colts would want a similar type of compensation package from teams looking to acquire Taylor, according to sources.

Taylor, 27, is under contract in 2027 for $15 million and in 2028 for $9.46 million, making him even more attractive to any acquiring team. Indianapolis already paid him a signing bonus of $15 million before the season.

But the Colts do not mind shedding salaries and players in exchange for draft picks. Over the past week, the Colts have traded Pro Bowl guard Quenton Nelson and Pro Bowl defensive tackle DeForest Buckner, netting a 2027 third-round pick, a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick. The Colts do not appear to be done.

They also have engaged in trade talks for wide receiver Josh Downs, who they have told teams is worth third-round draft pick value. The Colts have told teams that they want to hold on to Downs but are engaging in trade discussions regarding their wide receiver who requested a trade this past week.

Downs is expected to play Sunday against the Jacksonville Jaguars, as is Taylor, despite the Colts' willingness to deal both players for the right price.

Colts coach Shane Steichen addressed the trades with the team in a meeting, telling his players that while they all have love and appreciation for the players who were traded away, this is the business of the NFL and that he understands it. He asked the players to be professionals with how they handle it, and sources said practices have been solid.

But the business of these trades is difficult, especially for a new owner in Irsay-Gordon and an interim general manager, Ed Dodds.

After the Colts lost Sunday to the Vikings, there were said to be organizational conversations Monday spearheaded by Irsay-Gordon that led Indianapolis into the Nelson and Buckner trades on Tuesday -- with more potentially ahead.

articles.headline: Curry's ankle-breaker on Luka highlights Warriors' stunning 25-point comeback
articles.description: Behind a theatrical 31 points from Stephen Curry late Friday night, the Golden State Warriors roared back for a 112-95 win over the Los Angeles Lakers.
articles.headlineJa: カリーがルカを揺さぶるアンクルブレイカーを披露、ウォリアーズが25点差を逆転する劇的な勝利
articles.descriptionJa: 金曜深夜、ステフィン・カリーが圧巻の31得点を挙げ、ゴールデンステート・ウォリアーズがロサンゼルス・レイカーズに対し112-95で劇的な逆転勝利を収めました。
articles.body:
SAN FRANCISCO -- Behind a theatrical 31 points from Stephen Curry late Friday night, the Golden State Warriors roared back for a 112-95 win over the Los Angeles Lakers, becoming the first team in the past 30 seasons to trail by 25 points and win by at least 17.

Lakers star Luka Doncic was the story initially. His rematch against outspoken Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg dominated pregame coverage after Lendeborg criticized Doncic following their previous matchup and continued the conversation leading up to Friday's tip-off.

Doncic stayed quiet about Lendeborg publicly but responded loudly in an aggressive first quarter, putting up 21 points and five assists to jolt the Lakers to a 38-15 lead, shushing the crowd after "Luka sucks" chants broke out.

Los Angeles scored to open the second quarter, building that 25-point cushion, before the Lakers struggled with Doncic on the bench.

Two Warriors reserves, Georges Niang and De'Anthony Melton, combined for 27 bench points, making a batch of second-quarter 3s to zip them back in it and set the stage for Curry.

"Them boys had my back today," Lendeborg said. "Steph Curry did his thing."

Curry had eight points and three assists in a late second-quarter surge, hitting a deep 3 and a difficult layup before setting up Brandin Podziemski and Al Horford for 3s.

That completed the Warriors' 38-15 second-quarter response. In the shot clock era, this was the largest deficit ever overcome at the end of the first quarter (23) to be tied or ahead at halftime.

"What I would tell you guys is that 25, you know, it's the new 12," Warriors coach Steve Kerr said about facing deficits. "These games happen nightly in the league. I watched the Utah-Laker game today prepping. I think Utah was up 19 at the end of the first quarter and then the Lakers tied it by half. With the pace and the 3-point shooting, there's just these wild swings, and you just have to stay with it."

Curry scored eight more points in the third quarter and nine in the fourth, giving him 31 on the night and 75 over the past two games combined, as he begins to rev his engines in his 18th season.

The signature play of the night came with 6:27 left in the third quarter. The Warriors spent much of the second half hunting Doncic on defense, lining up screens to get him switched onto Curry.

Curry had Doncic isolated on the left wing and went through a dribble combination that sent Doncic into a misstep, causing him to tumble onto the hardwood as the fans rose.

Curry paused for a second, looked at Doncic, swished a 3, and then grabbed his face in celebration. Curry later told the Amazon Prime postgame crew that he "didn't expect it to get that nasty."

"There were people on the bench calling him a sicko," Lendeborg said. "I don't even know. It was astonishing."

Curry's performance, combined with a high-impact 21 points and six assists from Podziemski, shielded Lendeborg from what would have been a negative spotlight.

articles.headline: Where the 2026 Vikings rank among worst 6-0 NFL teams ever
articles.description: Aaron Schatz ranked the worst 6-0 teams ever by DVOA and point differential. Where do the 2026 Vikings land, and what's next for them?
articles.headlineJa: 歴代ワーストのNFL「6戦全勝」チームの中で、2026年のバイキングスは何位か
articles.descriptionJa: アーロン・シャッツがDVOAと得失点差に基づき、歴代ワーストの6戦全勝チームをランク付けした。2026年のバイキングスは何位に位置し、今後どのような展開が待っているのか？
articles.body:
Let's start with this: Only good teams go undefeated. It's one thing to win a game or two, but if you're starting 6-0, you're a good team. The Minnesota Vikings are undoubtedly a good team.

But not all 6-0 teams are created equal. The 1999 Rams beat their first six opponents by an average of 25.7 points. That is dominance. Compare that with this year's Vikings, who have won four of their six games by less than a touchdown.

So, are the Vikings the "worst" 6-0 team in NFL history? To answer that question, I used my proprietary DVOA (Defense-adjusted Value Over Average) ratings and simple point differential to look at every team that started 6-0 since the move to the 16-game season in 1978.

The good news for the Vikings is not only are they not the worst 6-0 team in the past 50 years, but that there's a team that was a little worse that won the Super Bowl.

Here's a look at eight of the worst 6-0 teams of all time, and what history says will happen next.

8. 2012 Atlanta Falcons

DVOA: 18.6% (ninth)

Point differential: +58

The Falcons started the 2012 season 6-0 by feasting on an unsustainable turnover margin. They had 17 takeaways in the first six games and turned the ball over only seven times. The Falcons picked up a 27-3 win over the Chargers, but also four wins by less than a touchdown, including a last-second 55-yard field goal they needed to beat the Raiders, who finished 4-12.

The Falcons were at least balanced in their good-but-not-greatness, however. DVOA ranked them ninth on offense, 11th on defense and 10th on special teams after six games.

What happened next: The turnover margin was, in fact, unsustainable. In their remaining 10 games, the Falcons had a turnover margin of just plus-3. However, they still went 7-3 over the remainder of the season. An easy schedule that ranked 27th in average DVOA of opponent helped. In the playoffs, the Falcons won a hard-fought battle over the Seahawks 30-28 but then fell to San Francisco 28-24 in the NFC Championship Game when Atlanta's attempted late comeback drive ran out of gas on the 10-yard line.

7. 1985 Los Angeles Rams

DVOA: 17.8% (eighth)

Point differential: +44

This team was surprisingly similar to this year's Vikings, driven by excellent defense (second in DVOA through six games) and special teams (fourth). Instead of a free agent quarterback from another NFL team, the Rams' offense was led by CFL star Dieter Brock in his only NFL season. Unlike the current Vikings, the Rams were a run-first team with superstar running back Eric Dickerson.

What happened next: The Rams shut out Kansas City in Week 7 and then stumbled, with a 4-5 record the rest of the way. That still gave them the NFC West title by one game over San Francisco. In the divisional round, the Rams shut out Dallas 20-0. Then, the eventual champion Bears destroyed the Rams 24-0 in the NFC Championship Game, and Brock went 10-for-31 with 66 passing yards.

articles.headline: NFL Week 8 predictions: Upsets, fantasy sleepers, stat lines, TD scorers, more
articles.description: Tough day coming for Derrick Henry? Browns pulling an upset over the Steelers? Fantasy potential for Geno Smith? Let's predict 15 things for Week 8.﻿
articles.headlineJa: NFL第8週の展望：番狂わせ、ファンタジーの伏兵、スタッツ、TDスコアラーなど
articles.descriptionJa: デリック・ヘンリーに苦戦が待ち受けているか？ブラウンズがスティーラーズを破る番狂わせを起こすか？ジーノ・スミスのファンタジーでのポテンシャルは？第8週に関する15の予測をお届けする。
articles.body:
Week 8 of the 2026 NFL season is underway after the Packers defeated the Panthers on Thursday night. But what will happen in the remaining 13 games? We have 15 predictions from our NFL experts.

First, betting analyst Pamela Maldonado picks two underdogs who could win outright. Then, analytics writer Seth Walder projects stat lines for three players. Fantasy football writer Eric Moody suggests three sleepers, and analyst Matt Bowen predicts three players who will find the end zone. Finally, analyst Ben Solak lays out four wild-card predictions.

Can the Browns pull off an upset over the Steelers? Could Ravens running back Derrick Henry have a rough stat line against the Bills? Is Jaguars tight end Brenton Strange a sneaky play in fantasy? And will Lions quarterback Jared Goff throw his first interception of the season? Let's make 15 big predictions for the Sunday and Monday action.

Jump to:

Upset picks | Projected stat lines

Fantasy sleepers, surprises

TD scorers | Other predictions

Maldonado predicts two upsets

Cleveland Browns +3.5 (+160 moneyline) at Pittsburgh Steelers

Pittsburgh's preferred way of scoring is by passing near the goal line, but Cleveland's defense has made those throws difficult this season. That could mean another afternoon of coach Mike McCarthy having to settle for field goals.

On the other side of the ball, Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson needs to get the ball out quickly and avoid sacks that kill drives. I'm taking the points because Pittsburgh hasn't shown enough offensive consistency to trust it to create separation, and Cleveland is capable of winning outright.

Baltimore Ravens +3.5 (+142 moneyline) at Buffalo Bills

Buffalo allows opponents to convert 45% of third downs, giving quarterback Lamar Jackson chances to extend drives instead of needing big plays every possession. His passing matters here because Buffalo is tougher against the run, and Baltimore's patchwork line hasn't consistently opened holes for running back Derrick Henry this season.

Quarterback Josh Allen will obviously challenge Baltimore, especially off play-action. But I don't trust Buffalo's defense to protect a lead. Assuming Jackson is healthy enough to play effectively after returning from a high ankle sprain, Baltimore can win this outright.

Walder predicts three stat lines

Alex Highsmith and Nick Herbig, Edges, Pittsburgh Steelers: Combined 2.0 sacks, 5 pressures, 5 tackles

Neither Highsmith nor Herbig has had the expected start to the season, with a combined 5.0 sacks and, even more surprisingly, below-average pass rush win rates at edge. But this Browns matchup provides an opportunity for each player to get back on track.

Both mostly play opposite the opponent's left tackle, who in this case is rookie Spencer Fano (15th percentile in pass block win rate). And they'll each be chasing down Watson, who has taken sacks at a huge 9.7% clip in 2026, the second-highest rate among qualified quarterbacks.

Laquon Treadwell, WR, Indiana

articles.body:
Barcelona midfielder Fermín López is an option to replace Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes, while Arsenal are interested in a loan move for Real Madrid striker Endrick. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Manchester United want to bring in Barcelona midfielder Fermín López, says The Daily Mail. United are reported to be in the market for a new No. 10, with the future of 32-year-old captain Bruno Fernandes up in the air after his public falling out with manager Michael Carrick. Lopez, 23, has had a good start to the season with five goals and four assists, and is considered an option, alongside Atletico Madrid's Pablo Barrios. Lopez missed Spain's World Cup triumph with a foot injury, but Barcelona would want around €80 million to let him go, with Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea also interested.

- Arsenal are interested in a loan move for Real Madrid striker Endrick in January, says TEAMtalk. The Gunners already have Kai Havertz and Viktor Gyökeres up front, but have struggled to score goals this season and the versatile Brazil international, 20, has not had many minutes under Jose Mourinho this season. Mourinho is reported to want Endrick to stay, but his representatives are exploring options for a move.

- Manchester United are looking to bolster their defense in the January and have interest is in Fulham's Calvin Bassey, according to TEAMtalk. Bassey, 26, has been in good form this season and was made Fulham captain. United will also be targeting a new left back and striker, after injuries to Luke Shaw, Patrick Dorgu and Benjamin Sesko, says The Times. Previous reports have linked the club with Newcastle United's Lewis Hall and AFC Bournemouth's Adrien Truffert, while up front Galatasaray's Victor Osimhen, Leeds' Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Crystal Palace's Jean-Philippe Mateta have also been mentioned.

- Barcelona will renew their interest in signing Inter Milan defender Alessandro Bastoni in January, says Mundo Deportivo. Bastoni, 27, was being tracked by Barcelona scouts with a view to the club making a €70 million offer last summer, but terms could not be agreed and the Italy international stayed put.

articles.headline: Michael Penix Jr. shows he could be Atlanta's QB1
articles.description: Penix has been mostly above average after 17 games as an NFL starter, and that's really all Atlanta needs him to be.
articles.headlineJa: マイケル・ペニックス・Jr、アトランタの正QBになれる実力を示す
articles.descriptionJa: NFLのスターターとして17試合に出場したペニックスは、概ね平均を上回るパフォーマンスを見せており、アトランタが彼に求めているのはまさにそれだ。
articles.body:
FLOWERY BRANCH, Ga. -- All Michael Penix Jr. wanted to do was get back on the field. That was the goal after he suffered a torn left ACL last November.

In the meantime, the Atlanta Falcons could consider him only a question mark. It was the quarterback's third ACL surgery. He had torn his right ACL twice in college. In 12 career NFL starts, Penix also had not shown quite enough to be considered a sure thing.

So, the Falcons hedged their bets. They signed veteran Tua Tagovailoa in the offseason after he was released by the Miami Dolphins and stated outright that he would compete with Penix for the starting job.

Fast-forward seven months and Penix, since his return, is working on turning that question mark into an exclamation point.

In Week 7, Penix helped lead the Falcons to a 29-20 win over the previously undefeated San Francisco 49ers, who had former Falcons coach Raheem Morris -- the man who helped draft him -- scheming against Penix as defensive coordinator. The performance earned Penix his first NFC Offensive Player of the Week honor.

"We were down 14-3 and he was great," Falcons offensive coordinator Tommy Rees said. "He was unflappable."

Atlanta has won three of its five games since Penix came back in Week 3. On Sunday, the Falcons (3-4) have a chance to reach the .500 mark against the NFC South rival Tampa Bay Buccaneers and move into a share of first place.

"When [Penix] is out there, this is a completely different football team, and I really truly believe that he's a franchise quarterback," Falcons safety Jessie Bates III said.

Penix has now started 17 career games, the equivalent of a full season. The raw numbers are not breathtaking, but they are good. Penix has completed 61.5% of his passes for 3,914 yards with 21 touchdown passes and seven interceptions.

If those numbers were applied to the NFL's 2025 season, Penix would have been eighth in passing yards and tied for 18th in touchdowns. The advanced stats tell a similar story. Since his rookie year, Penix is 17th in both EPA per dropback (0.03) and success rate (45.4%).

Those numbers don't necessarily jump out as elite. But they do establish a baseline. Penix has been at least as good as the average NFL starter in those 17 career starts.

This season those numbers have trended upward for the most part. Penix is ninth in ESPN QBR (67.1), 13th in EPA per dropback (0.09) and 19th in success rate (43.9%).

The Falcons don't need Penix to be the best quarterback in the NFL statistically. They just need him to facilitate things for an offense that has running back Bijan Robinson, wide receiver Drake London and tight end Kyle Pitts Sr. He has achieved that to this point.

"The goal is to win," Penix said. "That's been the goal from day one: win. We got to win football games, and we got the team to do it. We got the coaches to do it."

articles.headline: Joe Burrow's trust makes Tee Higgins level up for Bengals
articles.description: No receiver in the NFL has been better on tight window throws this season than the Bengals' Tee Higgins.
articles.headlineJa: ジョー・バロウの信頼がベンガルスのティー・ヒギンズを一段上のレベルへ
articles.descriptionJa: 今シーズン、タイトなパスコースへのスローにおいて、ベンガルスのティー・ヒギンズ以上に優れたレシーバーはNFLにはいない。
articles.body:
CINCINNATI -- When Tee Higgins sat alongside Ja'Marr Chase to ink their nine-figure contract extensions with the Cincinnati Bengals, the expenditures seemed like a luxury.

The two wide receivers' contracts totaled $276 million, a lot of money to commit to one position group. But over the past two seasons, they have given the Bengals their money's worth.

Chase has been a two-time All-Pro selection and is on the verge of being the most decorated receiver in franchise history. Higgins has been no slouch, either. Especially this season.

Through seven weeks, Higgins has been one of the NFL's most productive receivers. And as Higgins gets deeper into his career, this season has reinforced his standing on one of the league's most dynamic offenses.

"We're going to keep feeding him," said quarterback Joe Burrow, who added that getting the ball to Chase is also a top priority. "But the way that Tee's playing right now, it's hard not to throw his way."

Entering Sunday's game against the Tennessee Titans (1 p.m. ET, CBS), Higgins is fourth in the NFL in receiving yards per game (95.2). The seventh-year player is on pace for easily the best season of his career.

The value of what the 6-4, 220-pound Higgins brings to the offense has been apparent since the Bengals took him in the second round of the 2020 draft. And that specific style of receiver -- a tall, long player who can win on the outside -- is clearly something the Bengals favor. This year, Cincinnati used a fourth-round pick on 6-3, 218-pound wide receiver Colbie Young, someone Burrow said has the "same archetype as Tee."

But Higgins has proved this season why he has often been referred to as a "1B" option alongside Chase and is one of the league's best receivers in his own right.

According to Next Gen Stats, Higgins has been one of the top receivers on tight window throws. When a ball has arrived with less than a yard of separation, Higgins has a league-high 7.1 expected points added on catches in those situations. He has also caught six of nine targets into tight windows for 99 yards, one touchdown and no interceptions.

"When you're Joe Burrow and the ball's got to leave your hand, knowing that he's going to go get it and at the very least he's going to go protect it is a powerful thing," Bengals offensive coordinator Dan Pitcher said.

Sometimes Burrow has made up his mind long before most quarterbacks think about raising their arms to throw. For example, Burrow hit Higgins for a 19-yard completion against Baltimore in a look that seems absurd on tape. When Burrow started his throwing motion, Higgins was still several yards behind Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey. But Burrow trusted that he and Higgins were on the same page and fired the ball into the vacant space in the middle of the field.

"If it was somebody else, maybe I don't make that throw," Burrow said. "But I trust Tee and I know Tee's going to see exactly what I'm seeing and go and get that thing."

articles.headline: Michael Carrick: 'Hard truths' have been shared amid Man United slump
articles.description: Manchester United manager Michael Carrick said "hard truths" have been spoken between himself, the players and the club hierarchy amid an eight-game winless run.
articles.headlineJa: マイケル・キャリック：「マンUの低迷の中、『厳しい真実』が語られた」
articles.descriptionJa: マンチェスター・ユナイテッドのマイケル・キャリック監督は、8試合未勝利が続く中で、自身と選手、そしてクラブ幹部の間で「厳しい真実」が共有されたと語った。
articles.body:
Manchester United manager Michael Carrick has said "hard truths" have been spoken between himself, the players and the club hierarchy during an eight-game winless run that has left him fighting for his job at Old Trafford.

United face Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on Saturday aiming to win a domestic fixture for the first time since a 5-2 Premier League victory against Ipswich on Aug. 30 -- United's only league win so far this season.

- Tielemans backs Carrick to stay in Man United job

- Global power ranking: The top 20 soccer teams in the world, ranked!

- Carrick: 'Fully committed' Fernandes retains Man United captaincy

Last Sunday's 3-0 home defeat against Bournemouth, four days after a humiliating 4-1 Champions League loss away to Italian debutants Como, raised serious doubts over Carrick's United future before the 45-year-old was told by senior figures that he would remain in charge with pressure mounting to halt the dismal run of form.

But with criticism directed at his players and also CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox following their failure to sufficiently bolster the United squad this summer, Carrick said blunt conversations have taken place between parties in an effort to resolve the team's problems.

"It's pretty clear," Carrick told reporters. "It's not always rosy and nice conversations between anyone, whether that's between me and the players or whether it's between me, Jason, Omar or the owners.

"It's the truth, it's the hard truth at times and it's what we need to move forward. Whatever we need to move forward, we'll do.

"We always do what we think is going to get the best out of the team. Whether that's certain players that, of course, you speak to at certain points, that's normal.

"That's why, if you ask for leaders in the dressing room, you want opinions on certain things and there's going to be times when you ask that, that's fine.

"Absolutely no problem. It doesn't mean that we always agree with that, but absolutely no problem with that. And then we head off in the same direction."

United are in their worst run of form since the 1988-89 season and have made their worst start to a league campaign since 1986-87, when manager Ron Atkinson was fired and replaced by Alex Ferguson.

But Carrick said that much of the team's issues are rooted in a loss of confidence -- something he says can be rectified.

"Confidence is the beauty of sport," he said. "Confidence is in some ways the major factor of that belief, that self-belief, that confidence level.

"It kind of trumps everything else in terms of level of performance. But the beauty about confidence, it can come back quickly in one moment, one thing in a game, one win, one result.

"We've seen it before, we've seen it a few months ago, it can come back quickly. And that's what keeps you pushing and keeps you believing that it's always that close and what's possible is always within touching distance.

articles.headline: Achraf Hakimi scores 1st career hat trick as Luis Enrique makes PSG history
articles.description: Right back Achraf Hakimi claimed a first career hat trick and provided two assists as Luis Enrique became the winningest coach in Paris Saint-Germain history on Friday.
articles.headlineJa: アシュラフ・ハキミがキャリア初のハットトリック、ルイス・エンリケがPSGの歴史を塗り替える
articles.descriptionJa: 金曜日、右サイドバックのアシュラフ・ハキミがキャリア初のハットトリックを達成し、2アシストを記録。ルイス・エンリケはパリ・サンジェルマン史上最多勝利を記録する監督となった。
articles.body:
Right back Achraf Hakimi claimed a first career hat trick and provided two assists as Luis Enrique became the winningest coach in Paris Saint-Germain history on Friday.

The Ligue 1 leaders came from behind to thrash bottom club Le Havre 5-1 with Morocco international Hakimi playing a role in all five goals.

- PSG's Luis Enrique: Vitinha's Ballon d'Or ranking too low

- PSG star Kvaratskhelia undergoes successful knee surgery

He is just the fourth player with five goal contributions in a single game in the last four seasons in the top five European leagues. The last player to achieve that feat in France's Ligue 1 was Neymar for PSG in August 2022.

The result took Luis Enrique to 127 wins, breaking a tie with Laurent Blanc for most in PSG's history.

The reigning French and European champions briefly looked in danger of suffering a major shock when former Sunderland and West Brom forward Josh Maja gave the winless hosts an 18th-minute lead.

But captain Hakimi set up Mika Godts to level before completing the turnaround with a smart finish two minutes later and then curling home a fine 20-yard free kick early in the second half.

Hakimi, who had not scored this season ahead of kickoff, completed his landmark treble in fortuitous fashion in the 69th minute, after his through ball allowed Senny Mayulu to register the visitors' fourth goal.

The 27-year-old's first hat trick for club and country came in the 486th game of his career.

PSG's victory was their ninth in a row in all competitions -- and sixth successive league win -- after they picked up just a point from their opening three fixtures.

In the continued absence of key attackers Ousmane Dembélé and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia through injury, Luis Enrique made five changes to his starting XI following Monday's 2-0 success over Lyon.

Information from ESPN Research and PA contributed to this report.
